sentences.text:
And 4 Others
Counsel for Applicant :- Abdul Samad,Sunil Sharma

Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Subhash Vidyarthi,J.
1. Heard Sri Abdul Samad, the learned counsel appearing for the applicant and Sri Akhilesh Kumar Vyas, the learned Additional Government Advocate and perused the record.

2. By means of the instant application filed under Section 482 Cr.P.C., the applicant has challenged the validity of the order dated 21.1.2023 passed by the Judicial Magistrate-II, Raebareli in Criminal Case No.30311 of 2022 whereby the Magistrate has summoned the opposite party No.2 for trial of offence under Sections 498A, 323 IPC, 3/4 Dowry Prohibition Act and it has not summoned the opposite party No.2 for offences under Sections 504, 506 IPC and has not summoned the complainant's father-in-law, mother-in-law and sister-in-law who were also made accused in the compliant.

The applicant has also challenged validity of the judgment and order dated 07.11.2023 passed by the II Additional District and Sessions Judge, Raebareli dismissing the Criminal Revision No.4 of 2023 Smt. Minakshi Mishra vs State Of U.P. Thru. Secy. Home Lko.

entities.text: II Additional District and Sessions Judge, Raebareli
entities.label: COURT

entities.text: Criminal Revision No.4 of 2023 Smt. Minakshi Mishra vs State Of U.P. Thru. Secy. Home Lko
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
And 4 ... on 12 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/75322502/
1 filed by the applicant against the aforesaid order dated 21.01.2023.
3.

The applicant had filed a complaint against her husband, father-in-law, sister-in-law alleging that she got married to opposite party No.2 on 09.02.2019; that the accused persons were not satisfied with the dowry given by the applicant's family members and they were demanding additional dowry and were harassing her for pressing their demand.

It is further alleged that the applicant's father had given a car in the marriage and to meet additional demand, another car of higher value was given and Rs.7 Lakh was deposited in the bank account of the applicant's mother-in-law.

The complaint also alleges that the accused persons used to torn away the applicant's clothes, deprived her of food and whenever some meals were given to her something was added to it due to which the applicant often used to get unconscious.
4. In the impugned order dated 21.01.2023, the learned Magistrate recorded that prima facie offence of demand of dowry and harassment of the applicant was proved against her husband.
No particulars were given regarding the acts committed by the other accused persons.

5. Relying on the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme court in the cases of Geeta Mehrotra Vs State of U.P. & Kansraj Singh vs State of Punjab, the Magistrate found that no sufficient ground was made out for initiating proceedings against the other accused persons.

entities.text: Geeta Mehrotra Vs State of U.P. & Kansraj Singh vs State of Punjab
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
6. While deciding the revision filed against the aforesaid order dated 21.01.2023, II-Additional District and Sessions Judge, Raebareli relying upon the decision in the case of Kahkashan Kausar @
Sonam & Ors vs State of Bihar & Ors: (2022) 6 SCC 599 wherein the Hon'ble Supreme Court has held that "clearly demonstrate that this Court has at numerous instances expressed concern over the misuse of Section 498-AIPC and the increased tendency of implicating relatives of the husband in matrimonial disputes, without analysing the long-term ramifications of a trial on the complainant as well as the accused.

entities.text: II-Additional District and Sessions Judge, Raebareli
entities.label: COURT

entities.text:
Kahkashan Kausar @
Sonam & Ors vs State of Bihar & Ors: (2022) 6 SCC 599
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is further manifest from the said judgments that false implication by way of general omnibus allegations made in the course of matrimonial dispute, if left unchecked would result in misuse of the process of law.

Therefore, this Court by way of its judgments has warned the courts from proceeding against the relatives and in-laws of the husband when no prima facie case is made out against them."
7.

The revisional court found that the allegations leveled by the applicant are general and omnibus in nature and no specific allegations were leveled against her, father-in-law, mother-in-law and sister-in-law.
8. In these circumstances, the summoning order passed by the Magistrate did not suffer from any illegality and the same was affirmed by the revisional court.
9. While assailing the validity of the aforesaid order, the learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that the applicant has leveled specific allegations against all the accused persons.

However, a perusal of the complaint indicates that the complainant had leveled general allegations only and no averment was made regarding any specific act committed by the other accused persons with particulars thereof.
Some of the allegations leveled in the complaint which have been Smt. Minakshi Mishra vs State Of U.P. Thru. Secy. Home Lko.

entities.text: Smt. Minakshi Mishra vs State Of U.P. Thru. Secy. Home Lko
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
And 4 ... on 12 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/75322502/
2 mentioned above, prima facie appear to be unbelievable and it appears that the complainant has made an endeavour to entangle entire family of her husband to put pressure on them for arriving at some settlement resulting her matrimonial disputes.
10. Both the impugned orders are well reasoned order and this court does not find any illegality in the orders impugned.
11. The application lacks merit and is hereby rejected.
(Subhash Vidyarthi, J.) Order Date :- 12.3.2024
